attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data is now a dedicated XFS filesystem (loop-mounted from /var/lib/srv-data-backing/srv-data.img, persisted in /etc/fstab with the uquota mount option) enforcing a 100MB hard/soft filesystem-level user quota for datauser via XFS's native quota subsystem. Since the node's root filesystem is XFS mounted noquota and quota options cannot be changed via live remount on a running root fs, a separate quota-enabled XFS image was created and mounted at /srv/data instead of touching root fs boot parameters. Enforcement was verified both before and after a full node restart: writes past 100MB fail with "Disk quota exceeded", and the quota-enabled mount and limit configuration survive reboot via fstab.
